kinds.d: Hand-held fork with elastic bands that launches a small projectile. A toy one is in Toys & Games.

x.d: Ash-wood slingshot with flat rubber bands, strong enough for hunting and sold with an arrow rest.
Slingshot whose brace rests on the forearm to take high draw weights, powered by latex tubing; first made by Howard Ellenburg.

kinds.d: Pouch between two braided cords, whirled to hurl a stone or sling-bullet when one cord is let go.

x.d: Sling of the Balearic Islands, once made of rush or plant fibre and sinew in three lengths; still used in island competitions.
Braided camelid-fibre sling of the Andes with a wide central cradle and a finger loop, long used by herders.

v.d: llama or camelid wool; some up to 2.2 m

x.d: Short sling on the end of a wooden staff up to 2 m long, throwing heavier stones further.

kinds.d: Tube through which a dart is propelled by the breath. A toy one is in Toys & Games.

x.d: Japanese blowgun about 1.2 m long with no mouthpiece, shot at 10 m targets as a sport.
Southeast Asian blowpipe of 1.2–1.8 m, often fitted with a metal spearhead.
River-cane blowgun 2–3 m long, shooting darts fletched with thistle down or rabbit fur.

brands.d: US toy company that made an ash-wood hunting slingshot.

notes: Both old kinds kept; Sling added. Old slingshot models kept in m. Saunders/Trumark not named as wrist-brace originator: the slingshot-shooting.de Trumark page timed out (WebFetch and Firecrawl), so the archetype cites simple-shot.com, which credits Howard Ellenburg.
